html:
The Russian annexation of Bessarabia came in 1812, when the Treaty of Bucharest ended a Russo-Turkish war and gave Russia the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between the Pruth and the Dniester.

The Ottomans ceded land that was not theirs to give: Moldavia was a vassal principality. Russia named the whole territory Bessarabia and made Chișinău its capital. Russian became the language of the state, and Germans, Bulgarians, Gagauz and Jews settled the south and the towns. The region stayed in the Russian Empire until the union with Romania of 1918. The border on the Pruth drawn in 1812 is, roughly, the border of Moldova today.
